thread:
leila: kicking off porcupine embed bring-up. model=porcupine-int8 (per-channel). default run: 4-fold holdout, flat index vs PQ, no whitening. running recall + clustering + index-recall checks now.

andrew: nice — paste top-line when available, and a UMAP if easy.

leila: quick smoke CLI output:
```
$ run-eval --model porcupine-int8 --holdout=4 --index=hnsw+pq --metrics recall@1,5,10,hnsw_recall,silhouette,centroid_shift,anchor_flip_rate --cohorts=devdocs,short-query,longtail
recall@1: 0.695
recall@5: 0.845
recall@10: 0.889
hnsw_recall@1: 0.68
silhouette_avg: 0.36
centroid_shift_mean: 0.026
anchor_flip_rate: 0.0068
```
baseline (lucent-f16 float16): recall@1 0.74, recall@5 0.88, silhouette 0.52. so ~-0.045 @1.

carmen: yikes on silhouette. do we know if PQ is amplifying quantization noise or if the model embedding space itself is squishy?

leila: ran a flat-index (no PQ) control: recall@1 0.702, silhouette 0.39, centroid_shift 0.021. minor gain vs PQ — PQ seems to add measurable retrieval noise.

nik: try whitening + l2 renorm as an ablation — often recovers cluster geometry w/o hurting recall. also try per-tensor quant as a comparison to per-channel.

leila: ran whitening + renorm (same eval):
recall@1: 0.705
recall@5: 0.848
recall@10: 0.892
silhouette_avg: 0.47
anchor_flip_rate: 0.0031
notes: biggest improvement in devdocs + short-query cohorts; longtail unchanged.

andrew: that looks promising — silhouette up from 0.36 -> 0.47 after whitening. recall gap to baseline shrank to ~0.035. :+1:

carmen: request: per-cohort table and an anchor-level drift CSV (old_centroid, new_centroid_dist, uid). helps triage which anchors moved most.

leila: will attach. quick per-cohort delta snippets after whitening vs base-int8-without-whiten:
devdocs recall@1: 0.62 -> 0.67 (+0.05)
short-query recall@1: 0.74 -> 0.77 (+0.03)
longtail recall@1: 0.48 -> 0.48 (no change)
UMAPs saved for comparison.

eval-bot: artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-evals/porcupine/onboard/4411112222/ (umap_before.png, umap_whiten.png, per_cohort.csv, anchor_drift.csv, index_configs.json).

leila: next runs scheduled: 1) PQ re-tune (increase codebooks, larger subquantizers), 2) per-tensor vs per-channel quant compare, 3) microbatch/kv-cache shape sweep to align seq dist, 4) int4-fallback smoke.

nik: also add automated gating rules for canary: block if anchor_flip_rate > 0.005 or recall@1 delta vs baseline > 0.02 or silhouette_delta < -0.05.

andrew: +1 on gating. we should run the gating eval on a sampled warmup of real traffic too (to catch distribution mismatch).

carmen: PQ tuning might help latency/cost — but need to quantify recall loss vs storage. please include hnsw_recall curves vs ef/search and PQ params.

leila: noted. scheduling ef sweeps and PQ variants now. will post updated recall + hnsw curves in this thread. planning to create a short PR with run commands and S3 links once we have the PQ tuning run. :rocket:

eval-bot: follow-up task created -> eval-job-4411112222 (notify on completion).

leila: thanks all — ping me here if you want early access to the UMAPs or anchor CSVs for triage.
